reasoning: This was close. Set A has the stronger RL design and the more precise spec. It has a three-rung Snake ladder (tabular → DQN → full-grid CNN), ablations for memory, target network and exploration, a REINFORCE-vs-PPO claim, cross-play ratings with generations, exact tank physics numbers, and very concrete closed-form Snake golden cases (TC-01–TC-10 with explicit boards). It falls short on consistency and graph hygiene. The core is now built batch-first and team-aware from M1, yet CORE-06, the S2 outline ("deliberately revised shared core") and the fish idea's "the core is revised on purpose" still describe a later revision. M1-T26 requires the `net="cnn"` constructor to build a grid network that M1-T27 creates in parallel. M1-T21 repeats M1-T04's tank/predprey refusal. PL-01's table lists 16 'steps', most of them constructors that never appear in the five-line entry sketch. The docs are dense and jargon-heavy for a solo learner. Set B's spec and brief are plainer. Its pipelines are smaller and read more like call paths. Its spines are real baselines: online Q-learning before the replay buffer, REINFORCE before PPO. The method-check worlds (TRAIN-06) and the permutation-test definition are pedagogically sound. S2 is split well, with one fish → many fish → local sight each depending on the one before. B's main weakness is milestones. M1 can't watch a snake and doesn't require beating the baselines. M2 ("See, check and explain") bundles the DQN upgrade, replay, reference check and write-up, close to the leftover 'replays + reference' pattern. Its RL content is thinner (DQN only for Snake, no ablations, arena specs left 'tunable'). Overall B is a little more consistent, readable and buildable, and A is a little richer but rougher in its details.

strengths: Rich, pedagogically sharp ladders: tabular vs DQN vs CNN, ablations, REINFORCE vs PPO, three self-play rungs with cross-play ratings
Very precise spec with numeric physics and concrete closed-form golden cases
Library reference mapping pinned parameter by parameter (AD-04, AD-10, AD-11)
Three milestones, one per stage, each with checkable Exit criteria
weaknesses: Stale 'core revision' framing although the core is batch-first and team-aware from M1
PL-01 step table mixes constructors and is much larger than its entry sketch
M1 is very large: reference, ablations and CNN all in the first milestone
Dense, jargon-heavy prose for a learner

strengths: Clear small pipelines whose entry sketches match their step tables
Real baseline spines (online Q-learning, REINFORCE) that are then thickened
Method-check worlds and a fully specified permutation test protect against silent RL bugs
Fish tank split into one fish → many fish → local sight along real dependency lines
weaknesses: M1 delivers no replay and its exit doesn't require beating the baselines
M2 bundles the DQN upgrade, replay, reference check and write-up, close to a leftover milestone
Thinner RL content: no tabular rung or ablations; fish/prey physics left unquantified ('starting values the learner may tune')
Spine train_loop packet references WorldSpec/Policy without their definitions
